title: transitions.dev
freeNote: Free essential UI transition recipes (CSS/React + agent skills). Pro shimmer/recipes require paid tier—do not use without explicit approval.
agentUse: Pick a named free recipe (texts-reveal, number-pop-in, tabs-sliding, card-tilt, skeleton-reveal, success-check), adapt to product tokens, and always wire prefers-reduced-motion.

title: easings.net
freeNote: Fully free visual catalog of CSS/JS easing curves with copyable functions.
agentUse: Look up a named ease (easeOutCubic, easeInOutQuint, etc.) and paste the cubic-bezier or JS function instead of inventing timing curves.

title: cubic-bezier.com
freeNote: Free interactive cubic-bezier playground; compare against CSS presets.
agentUse: Tune a custom cubic-bezier visually, then copy the four values into CSS transition-timing-function or Motion configs.

title: Animista
freeNote: Free CSS animation playground with copyable keyframes; attribution appreciated, no paywall for basic export.
agentUse: Generate a small CSS @keyframes snippet for entrance/exit/attention, then simplify durations and respect reduced-motion.

title: Motion docs
freeNote: Open documentation for Motion (formerly Framer Motion). Library is free/open-source for standard use; check license for commercial edge cases.
agentUse: Read layout/animation/gesture APIs and copy idiomatic React Motion patterns rather than hand-rolling RAF loops.

title: animations.dev
freeNote: Public teaching site on web animation craft (Emil Kowalski). Course/paid material may exist elsewhere—use only free public pages.
agentUse: Study free essays on timing, easing, and restraint; translate principles into shorter product motion—not decorative loops.

title: Josh Comeau — CSS Transitions
freeNote: Free long-form tutorial on CSS transitions; some other Comeau courses are paid.
agentUse: Use as a mental model for transition properties, stacking context, and why duration/easing matter before adding JS animation libraries.

title: MDN — easing-function
freeNote: Fully free MDN reference for CSS easing functions including linear() and steps().
agentUse: Confirm syntax and browser support when emitting CSS timing functions; prefer MDN over blog folklore.

title: Lenis
freeNote: Open-source smooth scroll library; free to use under its published license.
agentUse: Only adopt when product intentionally wants smoothed scroll; otherwise skip—native scroll is often clearer and more accessible.

title: Paper Shaders
freeNote: Apache-2.0 open-source WebGL shaders (@paper-design/shaders). Free for commercial end products; pin versions (0.0.x may break).
agentUse: Install the React or vanilla package for mesh gradients, noise, halftone, etc.—prefer copy-friendly libs over inventing GLSL from scratch.

title: Maxime Heckel — shaders & craft blog
freeNote: Public teaching articles on shaders and real-time 3D for the web.
agentUse: Read a relevant post when implementing WebGL/R3F effects; extract patterns and cite—do not paste entire essays into prompts.

title: three.js examples
freeNote: Official free examples; MIT-licensed three.js. Study and adapt—do not dump entire demos into product UI.
agentUse: Find the closest official example for a 3D/shader need, then strip it to the minimal scene that serves the product job.

title: Codrops
freeNote: Free demos and tutorials for study; check each article’s license before shipping code. Inspiration-first.
agentUse: Browse demos for interaction/motion ideas, then rebuild a restrained product version—do not clone decorative Codrops chrome wholesale.

title: Open Props
freeNote: Free CSS custom-property design tokens (eases, shadows, sizes, gradients).
agentUse: Pull token names (e.g. --ease-spring-3, --shadow-3) into product CSS instead of inventing one-off values.

title: 21st.dev
freeNote: Browseable component/community gallery; treat as study material. Verify each component’s license before shipping.
agentUse: Search for a pattern (dialog, command palette, bento), study structure, then reimplement in the product’s design system—not copy-paste unknown license blobs.

title: Magic UI
freeNote: Some components are free/open; Pro packs are paid—use only clearly free/open components unless approved.
agentUse: Prefer free open components as structural references; skip Pro-only shimmer dumps and rebuild with Quiet Folio tokens.

title: Animata
freeNote: Free open hand-crafted interactive React components for study and reuse under project license.
agentUse: Lift a small interaction pattern (text effects, cards) and adapt tokens—keep motion short and reduced-motion safe.

title: Hover.dev components
freeNote: Public free demos of UI interactions; product/course offers may be paid—use demos as study only unless license is clear.
agentUse: Watch free demos for micro-interaction ideas, then recreate with product tokens instead of embedding their marketing UI.

title: Aceternity UI
freeNote: Many components free to copy; Pro tiers exist—stick to free listings and check license notes per component.
agentUse: Use free components as inspiration for layout/motion; strip decorative glow and re-theme to paper/ink before shipping.

title: React Bits
freeNote: Free animated React component gallery; verify license on each snippet before production use.
agentUse: Grab a minimal animated pattern as a starting point, then reduce intensity for product chrome.

title: Uiverse
freeNote: Community CSS/HTML elements; mostly free to use—check individual element terms.
agentUse: Mine for button/card hover CSS ideas; rewrite into the design system rather than pasting unscoped community CSS.

title: Origin UI
freeNote: Free open React/Tailwind component patterns (shadcn-style). Confirm MIT/project license before shipping.
agentUse: Copy structure for forms, inputs, and layouts; restyle to catalog/product tokens.

title: LottieFiles
freeNote: Large free animation library with license filters; paid assets exist—filter to Free and read each file’s license.
agentUse: Search free Lotties for micro-delight (success, empty states); prefer short loops and provide a static fallback for reduced-motion.

title: Lucide
freeNote: ISC-licensed open icon set; free for commercial use.
agentUse: Prefer a consistent open icon set over random SVGs; import only needed icons to keep bundles small.

title: Heroicons
freeNote: MIT-licensed icons from the Tailwind team; free for commercial use.
agentUse: Use outline/solid pairs for UI chrome; keep stroke weight consistent with the product type system.

title: Phosphor Icons
freeNote: MIT-licensed flexible icon family; free for commercial use.
agentUse: Pick one weight (regular/duotone) and stick to it across the product to avoid icon soup.

title: unDraw
freeNote: Free MIT illustrations; recolorable. No attribution required but appreciated.
agentUse: Use for empty states/onboarding only when illustration helps; recolor to brand and avoid generic stock-illustration sprawl.

title: Haikei
freeNote: Free SVG blob/wave/pattern generators for local craft; account features may vary—export free SVGs for backgrounds.
agentUse: Generate a restrained SVG background or divider, then inline or optimize; keep opacity low so content stays primary.

title: fffuel — nnnoise
freeNote: Free noise SVG/PNG generator on fffuel; other fffuel tools similarly free for local craft.
agentUse: Export a subtle grain/noise texture for paper-like surfaces; prefer CSS/SVG overlays over heavy image files.

title: Hero Patterns
freeNote: Free SVG background patterns; CC BY 4.0—attribute when required.
agentUse: Pick a light pattern, tint to paper/ink, and use sparingly as section texture—not full-page wallpaper.

title: Poly Haven Textures
freeNote: CC0 PBR textures—free for any use including commercial.
agentUse: Download CC0 maps (albedo/roughness/normal) for 3D or UI material experiments without license anxiety.

title: AmbientCG
freeNote: CC0 PBR materials and HDRIs; free for any use.
agentUse: Source seamless materials or HDRIs for local 3D/shader craft when product needs tangible surface detail.

title: design-slop-cop
freeNote: Public open-source kill-list tooling for common AI design tells. Citation only—no endorsement.
agentUse: Run as a second-pass checklist after taste review (vibe purple, glass, emoji grids); do not treat it as a substitute for craft judgment.

title: Rauno — craft notes
freeNote: Public craft essays (interaction, depth, novelty). Free to read; not a component dump.
agentUse: Read for interaction/restraint principles when refining UI; cite publicly available notes—do not invent quotes.

title: Emil Kowalski — Great animations
freeNote: Free public essay on what makes UI animation feel great; sibling posts cover restraint.
agentUse: Internalize timing/feel guidance before adding motion; pair with animation-restraint techniques in this catalog.
